question.text: The concept of 'determinacy' in an AIF trust ensures that:

answer.text: Each beneficiary's (investor's) share is clearly identifiable and ascertainable at all times
The trustee has unlimited discretion over distributions
The trust can invest in any asset without restrictions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.102-103) explains that in a determinate trust, each beneficiary's share is determinable distinctly, and the investor beneficial interests are ascertainable under the trust deed at all times. This is operationalised by dividing the corpus into unit capital and allotting specific units to each investor, so each investor's proportionate share is fixed by the units held. The Trap: Determinacy does not mean the trust is perpetual, that the trustee has unlimited discretion (that would describe an indeterminate trust), or that the trust may invest without restriction. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.102-103 (determinate trust — beneficiary share determinable distinctly; ascertainability via trust deed and unit capital).
